title: 41/128 route_v1 eval utterances are verbatim generation-prompt examples
detail: G1 injects each skill's catalog `examples` (skills/catalog.json:13-102) and G2/G3 inject the SPEC/CATEGORIES examples (prompts.py:64-84, G3 :40) into teacher prompts. 27 eval items equal catalog examples and 14 more equal SPEC/prompt examples, so 41/128 (32%) of evals/route_v1.jsonl are seeded into training generation; teachers echo them back. route_v1 accuracy will measure memorization of the eval set, and some echoes carry conflicting labels, so reported route numbers are contaminated either way.
evidence: Normalized exact match of evals/route_v1.jsonl@746450c vs catalog examples: lines 9,16,18,19,24,29,36,38,40,43,47,50,56,60,61,65,66,68,69,72,73,74,76,77,78,79,82 (27/69 catalog examples). vs SPEC/prompts quoted examples: lines 8 'a bit more',81 'undo that',88,89,99 'cut this',100 'set a timer',101 'text him',102,103,108,110,111,114,116. Generated sample training/artifacts/gen_sample2_picked.jsonl (1,080 rows) already has 15 exact eval hits, e.g. eval:50 'take a screenshot' (take_screenshot) generated as premiere_command; eval:80 'play it' (premiere_command) generated as ASK; eval:68 'play' generated as media_control AND premiere_command.
fix: Before any route number is reported: make eval and prompt examples disjoint. Either author a fresh held-out route_v2 (none of its texts in catalog.json examples, SPEC.md, prompts.py) and demote route_v1 to a dev set, or replace the 41 prompt examples with new ones. Add a postprocess assertion: normalized(utterance) not in {normalized eval utterances} else hard fail.

title: Spec 8-gram eval filter cannot match short items; no dedup/split code
detail: Word 8-gram Jaccard is undefined/zero for texts under 8 words: 100/128 route_v1 items and 542/1,080 sampled generated items are <8 words, so the specified filter removes nothing where leakage actually is (training-1). The branch has no exact-dedupe, MinHash, eval/HobbyLM-frozen filter or grouped 97/3 split code yet (git grep -nE 'minhash|dedup|97|val' training/src -> no hits; postprocess.py only writes route/args/rejects). Split grouping as specified (near-dup only) would also put the two contexts of one G3 text (postprocess.py:184-187 adds both) and future noise/follow-up variants of the same source on both sides of train/val.
evidence: Running the spec filter (word 8-gram Jaccard>=0.6) of gen_sample2_picked.jsonl vs evals/route_v1.jsonl: 0 removals; normalized exact match on the same data: 15 hits (see training-1).
fix: Eval filter = exact normalized match OR n-gram Jaccard with n=min(8,len(tokens)) (or char 5-gram Jaccard>=0.6) against evals/*.jsonl, HobbyLM data/frozen and DeskMind Bench texts. Split group key = (src call id, normalized text) so G3 pairs, noise and follow-up variants share a split. Add a test asserting zero normalized-text overlap train/val and train/eval.

title: G3 context pairs mostly mislabeled: 21/37 sampled items wrong
detail: G3 forces 'two contexts that lead to two different handlings' for every text, so gpt-5.4-nano invents a second label even when context changes nothing; postprocess.py:181 only rejects identical labels. G3 also emits arg-requiring skills with no args in the text (should be ASK). At full scale G3 is 3,000 examples (~6.5% of route data) with 0.6 weight on the intended (wrong) label, and several directly contradict G1 and the eval. Same sample also has ASK 9/30 fully specified (generated before the lead's ASK near-miss text change; re-check) and REFUSE 3/30 benign.
evidence: gen_sample2_picked.jsonl G3 rows (37): wrong = 'turn it up'->set_volume (no level), 'switch dark mode'->set_brightness, 'darker'->set_brightness, 'what's my battery?'@Calendar->todays_agenda, 'open downloads'@Safari->open_url, 'open this file'@Mail->open_url, 'open url https://example.com'@Finder->web_search, 'type hello'@Safari->web_search, 'search the web for cats'@Finder->find_file, 'make a new folder'->new_folder, 'trash this'@TextEdit->type_text, 'start a timer'->start_timer (eval:100 'set a timer'=ASK), 'add an event'->create_event and ->compose_email, 'set a reminder'->create_reminder, 'send a message to Alex'->send_message and ->compose_email, 'compose email to Jamie'->send_message and ->compose_email (no body), 'new note'->type_text, 'take a screenshot'@Premiere->premiere_command (eval:50 = take_screenshot). ASK wrong: 'Please switch to dark mode if possible.', 'Please open the Downloads folder for me.', 'Please turn Wi-Fi off for a minute.', 'What's my battery percentage right now?', 'Can you tell me my battery status, please?', 'Please center the front window.', 'Can you read my agenda for today, please?', 'Would you resize it to the right half, please?', 'Please take a screenshot and save it somewhere on the Desktop.'
fix: Let G3 return pairs only when handling truly differs (allow 'b': null, drop singletons); run A1 adjudication on 100% of G3 items (~3k Sonnet calls) and on ASK; postprocess: label an arg skill only if every required arg is present else ASK; reject ASK when nearest_skill has zero required args. Regenerate the 2% sample and re-post counts before full generation.

title: Runtime special-option descriptions differ from training: 0/50 token parity
detail: Runtime hardcodes short descriptions for MULTI_STEP/ASK/REFUSE/ANSWER, while training (catalog.py:36-37@746450c) uses skills/catalog.json special_options (lines 5-8). The route system prompt the LoRA is trained on is therefore not what the Mac renders: different text, 26 fewer tokens, and choice_pos shifts. Also both branches commit different files at training/artifacts/route_render_samples.jsonl (wip: id_list schema from runtime; cloud: header schema from training), so the AGENTS.md parity reference is ambiguous and will conflict on merge.
evidence: Re-rendering each wip sample's context+utterance with training route_render (uv sync --project training, Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B tokenizer): wip 0/50 token-identical, first diff at token 674, training render 26 tokens longer (stored 'needs several actions, apps or UI steps' vs catalog 'The request needs several UI steps or apps; hand off to the planner.'); cloud artifact 50/50 identical incl. choice_pos. training/tests: 3 passed.
fix: In decision.py options(): read descriptions from the catalog's special_options instead of the literal dict, e.g. `opts.append((s, self.catalog.special[s]))`; regenerate the wip artifact and add an ml test that asserts token equality with the cloud training/artifacts/route_render_samples.jsonl.

title: Teacher defaults to 397B on full set with no cost guard
detail: TEACHER defaults to Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, --limit defaults to None (whole route.jsonl), concurrency 64, and nothing estimates or caps cost before asyncio.gather; the SPEC 1.4 '$15 extrapolation -> 35B' rule lives only in prose. Each item is an independent sample_decision call; whether the 20% cached-prefill discount is applied is unverified. Route datums are ~803-817 tokens (artifact), not the ~520 SPEC 1.6 assumes, so training is also ~47% dearer than budgeted.
evidence: 45K route x 800 tok = 36.0M; 397B uncached 36.0M x $1.65/M = $59.4 (alone ~= Phase-1 cap); cached prefix (770 static tok @20%) = 45K x (770x0.33+30x1.65)/1e6 = $13.7. 35B: $16.2 uncached / $3.7 cached. Training/epoch: 36.0M + 25K args x 150 = 39.8M x $0.737 = $29.3 (SPEC: 27.1M, $20). Pilots 2 LRs x 4,000 items mixed ~2.2M tok = $3.2; val evals (1,350 x 800 tok prefill $0.33) x 11/epoch = $3.9. Phase 1 total: 397B uncached ~$96 (> $60), 397B cached ~$50, 35B ~$41-53.
fix: teacher.py: require --limit or --max-usd; before sampling compute est = sum(len(render_route(...).tokens)) x price (cached/uncached) and abort if est > remaining Phase-1 budget; default TEACHER to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B unless the 500-item pilot's billed cost (tinker billing) extrapolates <= $15. Update SPEC 1.6 sizing to ~800 tok/route datum.

title: Contexts sampled independently of label contradict context-dependent supervision
detail: Every G1 item gets a uniformly random app/selection (as SPEC 1.3 says), so context-dependent skills are trained in contexts where they are wrong, while G3 trains the opposite rule. The router learns to ignore app/selection, which G3 and the demo (Premiere vs Music 'play', 'copy this' with no selection) depend on. Separately, every sampled open_url request contains a literal URL, unlike speech.
evidence: gen_sample2_picked.jsonl: premiere_command G1 26/27 with app != Premiere Pro ('hit play'@Safari, 'could you undo the last thing I did'@TextEdit, 'add a marker'@Notes) vs G3 'play'@Music -> media_control; copy_selection 23/29 with selection=no ('copy this'); open_url 27/27 contain 'http' (eval:36 'open youtube').
fix: Needs a lead SPEC decision: per-skill context priors in contexts.py (premiere_command -> app=Premiere Pro >=90%; copy_selection/deictic 'this/that' -> selection=yes; type_text -> focused text field), or drop G1 items whose context contradicts the label. G1 open_url: spoken site names, no URLs.

title: ARGS targets fabricate unspoken values, incl. destructive move_to_trash paths
detail: G1 asks for args alongside heavy phrasing variation (indirect needs), and postprocess accepts whatever the teacher writes. ARGS targets contain values the user never said, so the ARGS model learns to invent file paths for a delete skill and message bodies the user did not dictate, and relative requests become absolute.
evidence: gen_sample2_picked.jsonl: move_to_trash 28/29 path args start with '~/' not spoken (e.g. 'the old draft, the one in Pages' -> path '~/Documents/old...'); compose_email 13/27 bodies with >50% words absent from the utterance ('Aunt Rose wanted to know if we're coming for the holidays.' -> body 'Yes, we're coming for the ho...'); 'Make it 10 percent quieter' -> set_volume level=90 (should be change_volume delta=-10).
fix: postprocess: reject/route-to-ASK items where any free-text arg (path, body, title, query) is not mostly (>=80% tokens) contained in the utterance; keep enum/number/datetime normalization; indirect compose_email without dictated content -> ASK (or drop); add a rule check that 'percent quieter/louder' maps to change_volume.

title: Adjudication verdicts never applied; 15% per-label STOP not computed
detail: collect() only attaches r['adjudication'] and writes *_adj.jsonl; nothing relabels/drops adjudicated items or recomputes target, and teacher.py:53 already blended 0.6*onehot(intended) for flagged items, so a 'teacher was right' verdict changes nothing in training data. The SPEC 1.4 per-label adjudication-rate report and >15% STOP gate are not implemented, which is the guard that would catch training-3. SPEC 1.3 ASR noise (30%, code) and 5% follow-up variants also have no code yet (only a style string at prompts.py:56).
evidence: adjudicate.py:59-73 sets r['adjudication'] and writes rows unchanged otherwise; git grep -nE 'adjudication\]|15|rate' training/src -> no consumer; git grep -nE 'noise|homophone|follow' training/src -> prompts.py:56 only.
fix: In collect(): compute per-label rate = flagged/total, exit non-zero if any > 0.15; apply verdict: label := verdict label and recompute blend(), drop 'ambiguous'/'neither'. Add noise.py (deterministic, after labeling, group id = source) and the follow-up rule generator before dedup/split.

title: ARGS datums bypass dedup/eval filter/split, leaking route labels
detail: dedup.py only processes route rows (keys on r['label']; args.jsonl rows carry 'skill', so --in args.jsonl raises KeyError) and writes only route_train/val. args.jsonl (1,353 rows vs 1,658 route in the 2% sample, i.e. most skill items have an ARGS twin) keeps every utterance, including those dropped for eval overlap and those assigned to route val. The ARGS user message starts with `Skill: {name}(...)` (route_render.py:39-41), so training on ARGS datums teaches utterance -> skill name for val and eval utterances: val route accuracy (used for LR pick and checkpoint selection) and any residual eval overlap are inflated, and ARGS exact match has no held-out set.
evidence: dedup.py:66 `k = (norm(r['utterance']), r['label'], ...)`; :125-127 writes route_{train,val}.jsonl only; postprocess.py args rows = {'skill','utterance','context','target','src'}; route_render.py:39 `ARGS_USER = """Skill: {name}({signature})`.
fix: Run args rows through the same pipeline keyed by (src, normalized utterance): drop args rows whose utterance was dropped from route (eval overlap/dup), and assign each args row the split of its route twin (same src+utterance); write args_train/args_val and report ARGS exact match on args_val. Add a test: no normalized utterance appears in both {route,args}_train and {route,args}_val.

title: Eval filter silently runs without HobbyLM tests and on stale route_v1
detail: HOBBY=/data/evals/hobbylm/data/frozen: if the clone is missing, glob() yields nothing and the run reports success with no HobbyLM filtering; nothing records how many eval texts were loaded. eval_texts() reads REPO/evals of the checkout it runs in, and cloud/data-pipeline still has the pre-ea64ce3 route_v1, so new route_v1 items are never filtered. Candidate retrieval uses MinHashLSH threshold 0.5 before the exact Jaccard>=0.6 check, which can miss true 0.6 pairs; brute force is ~128x45K comparisons and cheap. DeskMind Bench/macOSWorld/MacAgentBench task texts (AGENTS.md) are not included.
evidence: dedup.py:24 hard-coded path, :47-57 glob without existence check; git diff cloud/data-pipeline origin/main -- evals -> 43+/43- in route_v1.jsonl; :73 `MinHashLSH(threshold=0.5, ...)`.
fix: assert HOBBY.exists() and len(eval_texts()) >= expected (log counts per source into split_stats.json); merge main first; replace LSH with brute-force Jaccard over eval grams; add the other AGENTS.md eval task texts that are text-only.

title: New ctx contract makes Finder selection=yes unreachable; training uses it
detail: Contract now defines selection = focused element has non-empty AXSelectedText. Selected files in Finder are not AXSelectedText, so at runtime Finder selection is always 'no', while training labels Finder deictic requests by selection=yes (G3 'trash this'->move_to_trash, 'open this file'/'open the first result'->open_file). Those demo-relevant requests will be routed as the selection=no twin (ASK or another label). App names: the contract sends NSRunningApplication.localizedName (Act.swift:181) while training/eval use 'Premiere Pro'; whether Premiere reports e.g. 'Adobe Premiere Pro 2026' is unverified here.
evidence: AGENTS.md@a5e76fa:56-61; gen_sample2_picked.jsonl Finder selection=yes rows: 15/1,080 incl. 3 G3 items above; contexts.py:41 selection sampled independently of app; eval route_v1 Finder selection=yes: 0 (untested).
fix: Either define selection for Finder as non-empty AXSelectedRows/selected items in the contract (and HandsKit), or regenerate G3/G1 so Finder deictics don't depend on selection. Normalize app names to the training set in the app (map bundle id -> 'Premiere Pro') and add a route_v1 case with Finder selection=yes.

title: topk teacher gives every out-of-top-20 option the k-th logprob
detail: --method topk assigns each of the 36 choice ids missing from the top-20 vocabulary tokens the 20th logprob (an upper bound), so uncertain items spread spurious mass across ~16-30 absent options; e.g. 30 absent ids at floor -6 add 30*e^-6 ~= 0.074 probability that never existed, and after blending 0.4*teacher it flattens targets and inflates teacher entropy/ECE. Default is chunked (exact), so this only bites if topk is used to save cost.
evidence: teacher.py@4cbb74a topk_decision: `floor = min(got.values())`; `lp = torch.tensor([got.get(rendering.label_tokens[x], floor) ...])`.
fix: Renormalize over present ids only and give absent ids 0 (or floor - log(n_absent)); or keep chunked as the only method for soft labels.

evidence: Catalog v2 -> 41 options; route_render_samples@8c7c023 = 920-933 tok (mean 925.5, was ~805). chunked teacher: ceil(41/18)=3 requests/item. 45K x 925 = 41.6M tok. 397B: uncached 3 x 41.6M x $1.65 = $206; chunks 2-3 cached @20% = $96. 35B ($0.45/M): $56 uncached / $26 cached. Train 1 epoch (41.6M + 25K x 150 ARGS) x $0.737 = $33.4; + pilots $3.2 + val evals ~$4.5. Phase 1: 35B cached = $67 > $60; 397B cached = $137; 397B uncached = $247 > $150. Still default 397B, no pre-run estimate/abort.
fix: Default 35B + single-request scoring (topk with training-12 renorm fix, or chunk only the ids the top-20 misses); teacher-label a capped subset (e.g. 20K route items) instead of all 45K; pre-run est = items x tokens x (1 + 0.2 x (chunks-1)) x price, abort if > remaining Phase-1 budget.

title: Adjudication narrowed below SPEC; verdicts, STOP gate, ASR unwired
detail: collect() only attaches r['adjudication'] and writes *_adj.jsonl; nothing relabels/drops adjudicated items or recomputes target, and teacher.py:53 already blended 0.6*onehot(intended) for flagged items, so a 'teacher was right' verdict changes nothing in training data. The SPEC 1.4 per-label adjudication-rate report and >15% STOP gate are not implemented, which is the guard that would catch training-3. SPEC 1.3 ASR noise (30%, code) and 5% follow-up variants also have no code yet (only a style string at prompts.py:56).
evidence: adjudicate.py@8c7c023 select() (lines 37-47) sends needs_adjudication items only if label is ASK/REFUSE or the label's teacher-disagreement rate > 10%; SPEC:193 says every argmax!=intended & p>=0.7 item goes to A1, so confident teacher disagreements in other labels keep 0.6 x wrong onehot. Verdicts still only written to rows[i]['adjudication'] (line 62); no relabel/drop/target recompute, no per-label >15% STOP (SPEC:194). asr.noise still has no caller.
fix: In collect(): compute per-label rate = flagged/total, exit non-zero if any > 0.15; apply verdict: label := verdict label and recompute blend(), drop 'ambiguous'/'neither'. Add noise.py (deterministic, after labeling, group id = source) and the follow-up rule generator before dedup/split.

title: v2 relabel regex misses catalog's own lock/trash phrasings
detail: Existing v1 route items whose correct label is now lock_screen / empty_trash are found only by V2_RX; anything it misses keeps its v1 label (MULTI_STEP/ANSWER/etc.) while build_v2 G1 data labels the same phrasing lock_screen/empty_trash, so training gets contradictory targets and the router learns to split these intents. The regex misses the v2 catalog's own examples.
evidence: V2_RX = r"bluetooth|lock (the )?(screen|mac|computer)|empty (the )?trash" (relabel_v2.py@8c7c023:12). Checked: no match for 'lock my mac' (catalog example), 'clear out the trash bin' (catalog example), 'lock my screen', 'empty my trash', 'secure my screen', 'take out the trash'; and route_v1 eval items 'lock it up i'm stepping away', 'get rid of everything in the trash for good' would also be missed in training-style paraphrases. Finance relabel only covers MULTI_STEP items whose request style contains 'spreadsheet/finance' (line 20).
fix: Select candidates by score, not regex: run the v2 teacher (--in route.jsonl --differs) on every v1 item and adjudicate those whose argmax is a v2 skill; or at least widen to r"bluetooth|\block\b.*\b(screen|mac|computer|laptop)|\btrash\b.*\b(empty|clear|delete|everything)|empty .*trash".

title: Teacher guard assumes unverified 20% cached chunks; reserve short
detail: TEACHER defaults to Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, --limit defaults to None (whole route.jsonl), concurrency 64, and nothing estimates or caps cost before asyncio.gather; the SPEC 1.4 '$15 extrapolation -> 35B' rule lives only in prose. Each item is an independent sample_decision call; whether the 20% cached-prefill discount is applied is unverified. Route datums are ~803-817 tokens (artifact), not the ~520 SPEC 1.6 assumes, so training is also ~47% dearer than budgeted.
evidence: ca13466: default 35B, required --limit/--phase1-spent, pre-flight abort if est > min(60 - spent - 35, 12). $150 risk gone (teacher capped at $12). Residual: estimate() bills chunks 2-3 at 20% (teacher.py estimate) without verification; per item 925 tok est $0.000586 vs $0.00125 if uncached (2.13x), so a $12-est run (~20.5K items) really costs ~$25.6 -> Phase 1 = 25.6 + train $33.4 + pilots $3.2 + val evals ~$4.5 = $66.7 > $60. TRAIN_RESERVE=35 < train+eval ~$37.9; --phase1-spent is typed by hand (not tools/tinker_spend.py); 397B adjudication subsets and retries not reserved.
fix: Run a 200-item pilot, compare teacher_tokens.json est_usd with `tinker billing` delta, and set the cached factor from it; read phase1_spent from tools/tinker_spend.py; TRAIN_RESERVE >= 38 + 397B adjudication allowance.

title: Eval filter silently runs without HobbyLM frozen tests
detail: HOBBY=/data/evals/hobbylm/data/frozen: if the clone is missing, glob() yields nothing and the run reports success with no HobbyLM filtering; nothing records how many eval texts were loaded. eval_texts() reads REPO/evals of the checkout it runs in, and cloud/data-pipeline still has the pre-ea64ce3 route_v1, so new route_v1 items are never filtered. Candidate retrieval uses MinHashLSH threshold 0.5 before the exact Jaccard>=0.6 check, which can miss true 0.6 pairs; brute force is ~128x45K comparisons and cheap. DeskMind Bench/macOSWorld/MacAgentBench task texts (AGENTS.md) are not included.
evidence: 153a01c: decontam now includes evals/live_t1.jsonl (43 utterances) and logs eval_utterances per source, so a missing HobbyLM shows up in decontam.json, but nothing fails: HOBBY glob still unasserted (decontam.py eval_utterances), only *.tsv read; DeskMind Bench/macOSWorld/MacAgentBench texts still absent.
fix: assert HOBBY.exists() and len(eval_texts()) >= expected (log counts per source into split_stats.json); merge main first; replace LSH with brute-force Jaccard over eval grams; add the other AGENTS.md eval task texts that are text-only.

title: Stratified teacher subset skews label prior and mixes hard/soft targets
detail: --subset stratified teacher-scores all ASK/REFUSE/MULTI_STEP/finance_review/v2 rows but only 30% of every other skill. teacher.jsonl (the only file with soft targets) then has specials over-represented ~3.3x vs skills; if training reads teacher.jsonl the router's prior shifts toward ASK/REFUSE/MULTI_STEP (hurts top-1 on simple skills and ECE), and if it reads route.jsonl the 70% unscored skill rows get one-hot targets while specials get soft ones, so calibration differs systematically by label class (AGENTS: decision models train on soft labels). No trainer exists yet to settle which; confidence lowered.
evidence: teacher.py@153a01c: STRATIFIED_ALL = ("ASK","REFUSE","MULTI_STEP","finance_review"); STRATIFIED_REST = 0.30; `return [r for r in rows if r["label"] in STRATIFIED_ALL or r.get("v2_reason") or rng.random() < STRATIFIED_REST]`; run() writes only scored rows to teacher.jsonl.
fix: Sample the subset uniformly per label (same fraction for every label, e.g. 45% => ~$12 est), or keep stratified but write sample weights 1/p_label and have the trainer use them; decide one target type for unscored rows and apply it to all labels.

Against it via decontam.Index@153a01c: catalog examples 'take a screenshot', 'open youtube', 'turn on dark mode' are EXACT HobbyLM sealed-test items (they seed G1 prompts); SPEC/prompts.py example "I can't hear anything" ~ sealed-r1; the committed 2% sample has 8/1,080 hits (3 exact: 'open reminders', 'open documents', 'take a screenshot') -> ~330 of 45K route items. decontam only sees HobbyLM via /data/evals/hobbylm/data/frozen (unasserted), and when evals/external lands decontam.py:51 / dedup.py:45 do json.loads(ln)['utterance'] on every evals/**/*.jsonl -> KeyError on its 'text' rows.

title: ASR noise rewrites ARGS inputs but keeps clean copy-exact targets
detail: args_datums() passes noisy(utterance) into the ARGS prompt while r['target'] was extracted from the clean utterance. asr.noise strips punctuation and swaps digits<->number words, so 'open ~/Desktop/todo.txt' becomes 'open desktop todo txt' with target path=~/Desktop/todo.txt, and 'ninety seconds' becomes '90 seconds' while the target keeps the spoken form. That contradicts the ARGS system prompt ('Copy spoken dates, times and durations exactly as said; do not convert them') and teaches the 4B to invent paths, URLs and bodies that are not in the input (the training-7 failure mode). These ARGS go straight to native skills (open_file, open_url, send_message, start_timer).
evidence: Replayed asr.selected/noise('a:'+utterance) from 8f0b9bc on training/artifacts/gen_sample2_picked.jsonl: 214 ARGS items get noise, and 34 (16%) have a target value that appears verbatim in the clean utterance but not in the noisy input (fillers and false starts ignored). By arg: text 8, url 6, body 6, path 5, duration 4, start 3, end/due/title 3. Example: 'Can you open https://www.adobe.com for reference?' -> 'can you open https www adobe com four reference', target url=https://www.adobe.com.
fix: Apply noise only to route datums (noisy() in route_datums). For ARGS, either skip noise or limit it to fillers, false starts and a leading hey/please outside arg spans, and recompute number/datetime targets from the noisy text.

title: Pilot: finance_review val accuracy 0-25%, demo-critical skill
detail: finance_review is the demo's spreadsheet path (main's planner prompt says to prefer it). Both pilots score it worst of all 41 labels. Per-label val is computed on about 300 val items, so this is likely 4 items and noisy, but neither pilot gets it right more than once. The cause can't be checked from the repo (v2all data isn't committed). Plausible causes: build_v2 items overlap with MULTI_STEP, or the training-13 relabel regex left v2 items under old labels.
evidence: phase1_pilot-lr2e-4.md: finance_review 0.000, dark_mode 0.250, window_layout 0.500. phase1_pilot-lr4e-4.md: finance_review 0.250, dark_mode 0.500. Both: limit 4000, val_route 300, a single eval at step 31.
fix: Before the full run, post the finance_review/MULTI_STEP confusion and 30 sampled finance_review items from v2all with their teacher argmax. Raise val_route to the whole val split (about 3%) for the main run so per-label numbers mean something.

title: No val-based checkpoint selection: only the final checkpoint is exported
detail: do_eval() evaluates an anonymous save_weights_and_get_sampling_client snapshot. Only save_state at multiples of save_every (200) and the final sampler weights get persistent paths, and export/parity use the final one. With eval_every=50, the best-val step usually has no saved checkpoint. With one epoch that only matters if val peaks early, but the second-epoch decision is supposed to come from these curves, and an over-fit epoch 2 would then be the only exportable weights.
evidence: train.py:146 save_state only when step % save_every == 0; train.py:149 save_weights_for_sampler only '-final'; export.py:40-58 takes a single --tinker-path.
fix: In do_eval use save_weights_for_sampler_async(f'{name}-{step}') (the cost is just the save) and record the path in history; at the end export the argmax of val top1 (tie-break by ECE), never test.

title: mixed batches truncate to the scarcer datum type, silently dropping data
detail: With mode=mixed, steps = min(len(route)//nr, len(args)//(batch-nr)), and leftover items of the more plentiful type are never used. In a one-epoch run they are never seen at all, and the pre-flight steps/cost counts them as trained.
evidence: batch 128, route_frac 0.6 -> nr=77, 51 args per batch. At SPEC 1.6 sizes (45K route, 25K args): steps=min(584,490)=490, so 7.3K route items (16%) are never trained. At the 2% sample's ratio (1,658 route / 1,353 args): min(21,26), so about 21% of ARGS are dropped. Pre-flight n_steps = (R+A)//128 = 546.
fix: Cycle the shorter list (or pick nr per step by remaining counts) so every item is used once; compute n_steps from the same generator.

title: Adjudication narrower than spec; no 15% STOP gate

title: ARGS split defaults to train when route twin missing

Residual leak: rows whose raw utterance is not in route_dedup (exact-normalized dups dropped by dedup, A1 'drop', ask_args extras) default to 'train' even when their kept twin is in val. Downgraded to P2.

title: Phase 1 spend unverified; training alone exceeds TRAIN_RESERVE
evidence: 8f0b9bc: pilot tokens 2,444,167/4,000 items -> route ~925, args ~139 tok. Full 1-epoch run at SPEC sizes: 45K*925+25K*139 = 45.1M tok * $0.73 = $32.9; plus evals (~11 * $0.14 = $1.6) and two pilots (est $1.93 each = $3.9) = $38.4, which is over TRAIN_RESERVE $35 before the teacher. Phase 1 total = $50 if the teacher bills its $12 estimate, $64 at this review's $25.6 uncached estimate (over $60). Reports carry only est_usd; neither pilot report nor any commit records a `tinker billing` figure (SPEC:17 requires one after every run), so the cache assumption is still uncalibrated. train.py's --max-usd guard is separate from teacher.py's --phase1-spent.
